exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Can I Stay at Your Place?
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Tina: Hi Kerry, have you got a minute? I need a favour.
Kerry: Sure, Tina. What's up?
Tina: I have to leave my flat for two weeks while it's being painted. Could I stay at your place?
Kerry: I'm sorry, but two weeks is a bit too long for me.
Tina: Oh, I understand. I don't want to cause you any trouble.
Kerry: I'd really like to help, though. You're welcome to stay for a few days.
Tina: That's very kind of you. A few days would already help a lot.
Kerry: No problem at all. Just let me know which days you need.
exercises.translation_cn: 蒂娜请克丽帮忙:她的公寓要刷漆,得离开两周,想住到克丽家;克丽觉得两周太长,礼貌拒绝,但欢迎她住几天;蒂娜表示理解并感谢。

questions.stem: Why does Tina need a favour?
options: She has to leave her flat while it is painted.
She has lost the key to her flat.
She wants to sell her flat.
She is moving to another city.

questions.stem: How long does Tina need to stay at first?
How does Kerry refuse the long stay?
options: She politely says two weeks is too long.
She says nothing and walks away.
She tells Tina to find a hotel.

questions.stem: What does Kerry offer instead?
options: To let Tina stay for a few days.
To drive Tina to a new city.

questions.stem: How does Tina react to Kerry's answer?
options: She refuses to speak to Kerry.
She asks someone else at once.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Saying No Politely
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Being able to say no politely is an important part of emotional intelligence.
Always saying yes can leave you tired and unhappy.
A polite refusal usually begins with a few words of regret.
Then you give a simple reason and, if you can, offer another choice.
Refusing this way shows respect for the other person's feelings.
exercises.translation_cn: 能礼貌地说'不'是情商的重要部分;总是答应会让你疲惫又不快乐;礼貌的拒绝通常先表示歉意,再给出简单理由,可能的话提供别的选择;这样拒绝体现对对方感受的尊重。

questions.stem: Saying no politely is part of what?
What can always saying yes do to you?
How does a polite refusal usually begin?
options: With a few words of regret.

questions.stem: What should you offer if you can?
What does refusing this way show?
options: That you do not care at all.
Respect for the other person's feelings.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 I Heard What You Said
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Sam: Leo, I need to talk to you. I'm a bit upset.
Leo: What's wrong, Sam?
Sam: You told everyone what I said about the match. That was private.
Leo: I'm really sorry. I didn't think before I spoke.
Sam: I was just letting off steam. I never wanted the whole team to hear it.
Leo: You're right. I let you down, and I feel terrible about it.
Sam: Thank you for saying that. I still want us to be friends.
Leo: Me too. From now on, I'll keep your words to myself.
exercises.translation_cn: 萨姆因里奥把他私下说的话告诉了大家而难过;里奥承认没多想就说出口、辜负了萨姆,并真诚道歉;萨姆说他只是发泄,不想全队都知道;两人决定继续做朋友,里奥保证以后守口如瓶。

questions.stem: Why is Sam upset with Leo?
options: Leo told everyone what Sam had said.

questions.stem: What does Leo say about his mistake?
options: He did not think before he spoke.

questions.stem: What does Sam say he was only doing?
What does Sam still want?
What does Leo promise from now on?
options: To keep Sam's words to himself.
To tell more people the news.
To never speak to Sam again.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 The Truth About White Lies
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Many people tell small white lies to protect the feelings of others.
We might say a meal is delicious even when we do not like it.
Sometimes we lie to avoid another person's disappointment.
But honest, kind comments can help a friend improve.
In the end, the truth is often the kinder choice.
exercises.translation_cn: 许多人为保护他人感受而说善意的小谎;我们也许会说一顿饭很好吃,即使并不喜欢;有时撒谎是为了避免对方失望;但诚实而善意的评价能帮朋友进步;归根结底,真话往往是更善良的选择。

questions.stem: Why do many people tell white lies?
options: To protect the feelings of others.

questions.stem: What example of a white lie is given?
options: Saying a meal is delicious when it is not.

questions.stem: Sometimes we lie to avoid what?
What can honest, kind comments do?
What does the speaker say about the truth in the end?
options: It is always too hard to say.
It is often the kinder choice.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Thanks, but No Thanks
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mike: Hi Ryan, would you like to come to a boxing match on Saturday?
Ryan: That's kind of you, Mike, but I'm afraid I can't.
Mike: Oh, why not? It'll be exciting.
Ryan: To be honest, I don't really enjoy boxing. I hope you understand.
Mike: Of course. Thanks for being honest with me.
Ryan: Maybe we could watch a film together next week instead?
Mike: That sounds great. I'd like that much more anyway.
Ryan: Perfect. Let's plan it for next Saturday then.
exercises.translation_cn: 迈克邀瑞安周六看拳击赛;瑞安礼貌地说自己其实不喜欢拳击,委婉拒绝并希望迈克理解;迈克感谢他的坦诚;瑞安提议下周一起看电影代替,迈克欣然接受。

questions.stem: What does Mike invite Ryan to do?
options: Watch a boxing match on Saturday.

questions.stem: Why does Ryan refuse?
options: He does not really enjoy boxing.

questions.stem: How does Mike react to Ryan's honest answer?
options: He thanks Ryan for being honest.

questions.stem: What does Ryan suggest doing instead?
How does Mike feel about the new plan?

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 The Porcupines' Distance
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: On a cold night, a group of porcupines moved together to keep warm.
But their sharp spines hurt one another, so they had to move apart.
After trying again and again, they found the perfect distance.
It was close enough for warmth but far enough to stay safe.
This story reminds us that good friendships also need a little space.
exercises.translation_cn: 寒夜里,一群豪猪挤在一起取暖;可身上的尖刺会扎到彼此,只好分开;一次次尝试后,它们找到了完美的距离——既能取暖又不会受伤;这个故事提醒我们,好的友谊也需要一点空间。

questions.stem: Why did the porcupines move together?
options: To keep warm on a cold night.

questions.stem: Why did they have to move apart?
options: Their sharp spines hurt one another.

questions.stem: What did they find after trying again and again?
What was special about that distance?
options: It was too far to feel warm.
It was too close to be safe.
It kept them cold all night.

questions.stem: What does the story remind us about friendships?
options: They need no effort at all.
They also need a little space.
